questions.prompt: What does `set -euo pipefail` enable at the top of a Bash script?

options.text: Exit on non-zero command (`-e`), error on unset variables (`-u`), and fail a pipeline if any stage fails (`-o pipefail`)

questions.prompt: Under `set -e`, when does a failing command NOT cause the script to exit?

options.text: When part of an `if`/`while` condition, left side of `&&`/`||`, negated with `!`, or in `cmd || true`

questions.prompt: What subtle `set -e` trap happens with `(( count++ ))` when `count` is `0`?

options.text: Post-increment `(( count++ ))` evaluates to `0`, which makes `(( ... ))` return exit status `1` and abort under `set -e` (use `(( ++count ))` or `count=$((count + 1))`)

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `trap` in Bash. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `trap` can clean up temporary files created with `mktemp` reliably
Multiple signals can be trapped at once (`trap cleanup INT TERM EXIT`)
`trap` runs in a separate OS thread while the script continues
`trap cleanup EXIT` runs `cleanup` whether the script exits normally, fails under `set -e`, or exits via `exit N`

questions.prompt: Match each Bash `set` / `shopt` option to its effect.

columns.label: Unmatched globs like `*.xyz` expand to nothing instead of literal `'*.xyz'`
Pipeline exit status is the rightmost non-zero command (not just the last command)
Prevents `>` from accidentally overwriting an existing file (use `>|` to force)

questions.prompt: Why is `mktemp -d` preferred over hardcoded `/tmp/myscript_tmp`?

options.text: `mktemp` creates a unique, unpredictable path with `0700`/`0600` permissions, preventing symlink/TOCTOU race attacks and concurrent run collisions

questions.prompt: What does `"${PIPESTATUS[@]}"` contain immediately after `cmd1 | cmd2 | cmd3`?

options.text: An array of the individual exit codes of `cmd1`, `cmd2`, and `cmd3`

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `( cmd1; cmd2 )` and `{ cmd1; cmd2; }`?

options.text: `(...)` runs in a child subshell (variable/dir changes stay isolated); `{ ...; }` runs in the current shell

questions.prompt: Why is storing a command in a string `cmd="curl -H 'Auth: x'"` and running `$cmd` broken, and how do you fix it?

options.text: Quotes inside `$cmd` become literal characters, not syntax; store args in an array `cmd=(curl -H 'Auth: x')` and run `"${cmd[@]}"`

questions.prompt: What does `set -x` (xtrace) do, and how can you customize it for debugging?

options.text: Prints each expanded command to `stderr` before executing it (customize prefix with `PS4='+ ${BASH_SOURCE}:${LINENO}: '`, beware leaking secrets!)

questions.prompt: What does `bash -n script.sh` do?

options.text: Parses `script.sh` and checks for syntax errors without executing any commands

questions.prompt: What does `shellcheck` catch that `bash -n` does not?

options.text: Unquoted expansions (`$var`), `SC2046` word splitting, useless `cat`, `local x=$(cmd)` masking exit codes, and POSIX mismatches

questions.prompt: Why does `local out=$(failing_cmd)` mask `failing_cmd`'s non-zero exit code even under `set -e`?

options.text: The `local` builtin itself returns exit status `0`, overriding `failing_cmd`'s exit status! Declare `local out` on one line and `out=$(failing_cmd)` on the next

questions.prompt: Select all best practices for handling user/external input safely in Bash. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Never pass untrusted strings to `eval`, `sh -c`, or `awk`/`sed` code arguments

questions.prompt: What does `flock -n 9 || exit 1` inside `( flock -n 9 || exit 1; ... ) 9>/var/lock/job.lock` accomplish?

options.text: Acquires a non-blocking exclusive advisory file lock on fd 9 so overlapping cron runs exit immediately instead of racing

questions.prompt: What does `exec 3>"$logfile"` do in a Bash script?

options.text: Opens `$logfile` on custom file descriptor 3 for the rest of the shell's lifetime (write via `>&3`, close via `exec 3>&-`)

questions.prompt: What does `wait "$pid"` do when running background jobs (`cmd & pid=$!`)?

options.text: Waits for background job `$pid` to finish and returns its exit status (propagating failures)

questions.prompt: What does `wait -n` (Bash 4.3+) do when multiple background jobs are running?

options.text: Waits for the *next* single background job to complete and returns its exit status (great for worker pools / fail-fast)

questions.prompt: Why can `IFS=$'\n\t'` be problematic if left modified globally in a script?

options.text: Functions or sourced libraries expecting default space-splitting may behave unexpectedly; prefer scoping `IFS=` locally (e.g., `IFS= read -r`)

questions.prompt: Match each Bash strict-mode or safety pitfall to its fix.
What does `shopt -s globstar` enable in Bash 4+?

options.text: Recursive `**` globbing matching zero or more directories (`**/*.ts`)

questions.prompt: What happens when `[[ "$a" == "$b" ]]` vs `[[ "$a" == $b ]]` is evaluated?

options.text: Quoted `"$b"` checks literal string equality; unquoted `$b` treats `*`, `?`, `[...]` inside `$b` as a glob pattern!

questions.prompt: What is the risk of `rm -rf "$DIR/"*` if `$DIR` is accidentally empty?

options.text: If `$DIR` is empty, it expands to `rm -rf /*`! Always guard with `"${DIR:?}"` or `[[ -n "$DIR" ]]`

questions.prompt: What does `coproc` in Bash 4+ create?

options.text: A co-process running asynchronously with two-way pipes connected via `${COPROC[0]}` and `${COPROC[1]}`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about signals and process termination in Bash. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `SIGKILL` runs the script's `trap ... EXIT` handler cleanly
`SIGTERM` (15) asks a process to terminate gracefully and can be caught by `trap`
`SIGKILL` (9) forces immediate kernel termination and CANNOT be caught or ignored
`kill -0 "$pid"` checks if process `$pid` exists and can receive signals without killing it

questions.prompt: What does `exec "$@"` at the end of a Docker `entrypoint.sh` script accomplish?

options.text: Replaces the shell process (PID 1) with the target command so signals (`SIGTERM`) go directly to the application

questions.prompt: What does `set -o errexit` do inside a command substitution `x=$(false; echo hi)` by default?

options.text: In Bash (unless `shopt -s inherit_errexit` is set in 4.4+), subshells in `$()` may NOT inherit `errexit` if part of a larger expression or older behavior

questions.prompt: What does `readarray -d '' files < <(find . -type f -print0)` do?

options.text: Reads NUL-delimited filenames from `find -print0` safely into the `files` array (Bash 4.4+)

questions.prompt: What is a classic pitfall of `cat file | grep foo > file`?

options.text: The shell truncates `file` to 0 bytes via `> file` *before* `cat` even starts reading it, destroying the file!

questions.prompt: How can you atomically update a config file `cfg.json` from a Bash script?

options.text: Write to a temp file in the *same directory/filesystem* (`tmp=$(mktemp "${cfg}.XXXXXX")`) and `mv -- "$tmp" "$cfg"`

questions.prompt: What does `"${@:2}"` expand to?

options.text: All positional arguments starting from `$2` onward, each properly quoted

questions.prompt: What does `declare -p my_var` print?

options.text: The exact `declare` statement showing attributes (`-a`, `-A`, `-r`, `-x`) and value—invaluable for debugging Bash types

questions.prompt: Match each Bash diagnostic/safety tool or pattern to its role.

columns.label: Static analysis linting for quoting, subshell, and POSIX bugs
Prints destructive operations without executing them

questions.prompt: What does `umask 077` set for newly created files/directories in a script?

options.text: Restricts new files/dirs to owner-only access (`700` dirs / `600` files), protecting sensitive artifacts

questions.prompt: What happens when `trap` catches `ERR` without `set -o errtrace` (`set -E`)?

options.text: Functions and subshells do NOT inherit the `ERR` trap unless `set -E` is enabled

questions.prompt: What does `printf -v formatted '%04d' "$num"` do?

options.text: Assigns the formatted zero-padded string directly into variable `formatted` without spawning a `$()` subshell

questions.prompt: Select all scenarios where you should switch from Bash to Python, Go, or Rust instead of stretching a shell script. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: High-throughput parsing or concurrent network/API orchestration
Simple 10-line wrapper invoking 2–3 system binaries in a Makefile
Complex nested data structures, JSON/YAML transformations, or stateful retries
Cross-platform Windows/Linux/macOS CLI distribution without POSIX tool differences

questions.prompt: Why is `[[ $x -eq 1 ]]` vs `(( x == 1 ))` dangerous if `$x` comes from untrusted input?

options.text: Both `-eq` and `(( ... ))` evaluate `$x` as an arithmetic expression—meaning `x='a[$(id>&2)]'` can execute arbitrary commands!

questions.prompt: What does `set -o noglob` (`set -f`) prevent?
What does `compgen -G '*.json'` or `shopt -s nullglob` avoid when checking if any `.json` files exist?

options.text: Treating the literal string `'*.json'` as a filename when zero `.json` files match

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `BATS` (Bash Automated Testing System). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Provides `run cmd` to capture `$status` and `$output` without aborting on non-zero exit
Integrates with CI to prevent regressions in shell scripts
Requires compiling Bash scripts to C
Lets you write unit and integration tests for Bash scripts using `@test "description" { ... }`

questions.prompt: What does `exec 19>"$TRACE_LOG"; BASH_XTRACEFD=19; set -x` accomplish in Bash 4.1+?

options.text: Routes `set -x` trace output to fd 19 (`$TRACE_LOG`) instead of polluting `stderr` of the script's output
